images.caption: Figure 1:WorldRuler enables persistent, rule-governed generative worlds.The saved rules and world state allow the player to collect the key and open the door after loading, demonstratingRule-State PersistenceandRule-to-Visual Realization.

Figure 2:Overview of WorldRuler.
Rule execution updates persistent object states, dynamic binding associates rule entities with 3D instances and their current image regions, and local attribute replacement corrects denoising estimates for the next sampling update.
Rules, states, execution progress, and bindings are saved and restored jointly.
Independent perceptual feedback informs subsequent windows.
Scene and point cloud images come from the demo visualization, while the remaining flows and gate-state comparison illustrate the mechanism.

Figure 3:Local attribute replacement and paired training.
(a) A frozen reader estimates current attributes, and rule targets determine their discrepancies.
Attribute corrections and compatible adjustments modify local features before insertion into the sampling update.
(b) Counterfactual reconstruction supervises two target states and their difference from shared generated features.
Bidirectional swapping starts from real paired features and supervises replacement with the other state.
All branches share the replacement operatorTϕT_{\phi}. Dashed links indicate supervision.

Figure 4:RuleVerse data collection. Scene capabilities constrain rule and script authoring, and compiled actions are executed with the designated rules enabled and disabled.
Simulator states and events provide annotations of rule outcomes.
Videos and annotations are checked before splitting by scene or location group.

Figure 6:Qualitative results on the GTA-V subset of RuleVerse from the WorldRuler runtime with MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA. The two cases show fire and smoke after shooting a fuel tank, and smoke after entering a vehicle. Enabled and disabled branches are displayed at matching video times, with red boxes marking visible effect regions.
